---
title: "$ completes names for you"
ref: IDX-02
categories: [Indexing]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'list(alpha = 0.05)$a'
reponse: '0.05'
attendu: "`NULL`, there is no element named a"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno, hadley/strict"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
settings <- list(alpha = 0.05)
settings$a
settings[["a"]]

results <- data.frame(revenue = 10)
results$rev
```
:::

## Why

On a list, `$` accepts a prefix: if only one name starts with `a`, that element is returned, without warning. `[[` requires the exact name. A data frame column behaves the same way: `results$rev` returns the `revenue` column.

The day someone adds an `amplitude` element to the list, `settings$a` starts returning `NULL`, and the code that depends on it changes behaviour although nobody touched it.

## The fix

Use `[[` in production code, or ask R to flag every partial match.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
options(warnPartialMatchDollar = TRUE)
settings$a
```
:::
